subject.title: Feature/Fix: Add conservative lineage safety and promotion controls

question: Should CodexBar adopt this four-PR lineage-accounting architecture, or land the narrower fork-identity and cache-invalidation repair at https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118 first and reassess the broader design afterward?
rationale: Both paths address the linked overcount investigation, but they differ materially in scope, cache model, long-term maintenance cost, and rollout risk; tests cannot determine which architecture the project intends to own.

options.title: Land narrow repair first
options.body: Merge the smaller positively proven correction, measure the remaining failures, and keep this architecture pending only if those failures demonstrate a need for lineage authority.

options.title: Adopt lineage stack
options.body: Confirm the architecture, merge its dependencies in order, and require exact-head frozen-corpus proof for promotion, fallback, upgrade, and rollback behavior before this PR lands.

options.title: Keep shadow-only research
options.body: Retain lineage accounting as non-authoritative instrumentation while deferring the selector and promotion path until longer-running evidence establishes operational safety.

recommendation.title: Land narrow repair first
recommendation.body: Merge the smaller positively proven correction, measure the remaining failures, and keep this architecture pending only if those failures demonstrate a need for lineage authority.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice establishes the permanent Codex accounting and cache architecture, making repository-owner product direction the decisive signal.
